beats.say: In 1279 the Mamluks seize Cairo, ending Ayyubid rule and establishing a warrior-led sultanate.
At Ain Jalut in 1260 the Mamluks halt the Mongol advance, securing the Levant for centuries.
In 1396 the Mamluks join the Ottoman victory at Nicopolis, demonstrating their pivotal role against European crusaders.
By 1516 the Ottoman cannon crushes the Mamluk army at Marj Dabiq, ending their Syrian dominance.
By 1517 the Ottomans absorb Egypt, transforming the Mamluk Sultanate into provincial governors under Istanbul.
Yet the Mamluk military ethos lives on, shaping Egypt's modern officer corps and elite cavalry traditions.
